_about: Corrections the Rig Card makes when it imports CastAI's library (scripts/import-castai-library.mjs). Keyed by CastAI file and id. 'set' uses CastAI's own field names and format, so the CastAI lane can paste it upstream. When CastAI ships the fix, delete the entry here and rerun the import. docs/castai-library-fixes.md is written from this file.

set.tips: Use 8 wraps on braid and 5 to 6 on mono or fluoro. Braid is slippery and needs more wraps, not fewer.
steps: Step 1: Thread about 8 inches of line through the hook eye
Step 2: Bring the tag end back alongside the standing line so they run parallel
Step 3: Curve the tag end back toward the hook to make a loop that crosses over both parallel lines
Step 4: Wrap the tag end through the loop and around both lines 5 to 6 times (8 on braid), working away from the hook
Step 5: Wet the knot, then pull the tag end to snug the wraps into a neat coil
Step 6: Pull the standing line to slide the knot tight against the hook eye
Step 7: Trim the tag end

FishingKnots/uni.reason: CastAI says braid needs fewer wraps (5) than mono (6) because it is slipperier. That is backwards: slippery braid needs more wraps. CastAI's own Double Uni card says 8 on braid. The steps say 5 to 6 wraps with no word on braid, though the card is for braid too.
FishingKnots/uni.source: CastAI FishingKnots.json double-uni tips; Fishthatwontquit uni knot video (f1pFMWc0ZP0)

set.description: A snell with a loop at the eye. The loop clamps a roe cluster, yarn or bait to the hook so it stays on the cast.
set.bestFor: Holding roe, yarn or bait on the hook for salmon and steelhead
steps: Step 1: Pass the end of the leader through the eye toward the bend. Pinch a short end along the shank
Step 2: Wrap the long end tight around the shank and the short end 10 times, from the eye toward the bend
Step 3: Pass the long end back through the eye from the bend side, the opposite way to the first pass
Step 4: Use the loop this makes to wrap 5 more times toward the bend
Step 5: Pull the long end slowly to seat the wraps
Step 6: Push a little line back through the eye to open the loop, set the roe in it, and pull the leader to clamp it
set.tips: Bait hooks only. Pre-snelled egg loop hooks come tied, and beat tying one in the cold.

FishingKnots/egg-loop-knot.reason: CastAI calls it a fly fishing knot whose loop hangs below the hook, and its steps do not tie an egg loop. It is a bait snell: the long end, the one to the swivel, wraps the shank and the short end, goes back through the eye the opposite way, and a loop pushed back through the eye clamps the roe. No video in CastAI.
FishingKnots/egg-loop-knot.source: netknots.com/fishing_knots/egg-loop; animatedknots.com/egg-loop-knot ('Wrap the long end around the hook and short end'); theknotsmanual.com egg loop knot; video: Fishthatwontquit egg loop (hNcNZpyyHF8)

steps: Step 1: Tie a loose overhand knot about 5 inches from the end of the line
Step 2: Pass the tag through the lure eye and back through the overhand knot
Step 3: Wrap the tag 3 times around the standing line
Step 4: Pass the tag back through the overhand knot, then through the loop you just made
Step 5: Wet it and pull the standing line, the tag and the loop to tighten
Step 6: Trim the tag

FishingKnots/rapala-knot.reason: CastAI ties the overhand after threading the eye and leaves out the last pass through the loop, which is what locks the knot. No video in CastAI.
FishingKnots/rapala-knot.source: animatedknots.com/rapala-knot; Salt Strong Rapala knot video (OmeEudIttCI)

FishingKnots/rapala-loop.reason: The Rapala loop is the Rapala knot under its fly fishing name, with the same steps. One card, and its name finds it.
FishingKnots/rapala-loop.source: animatedknots.com/rapala-knot; Fulling Mill, How To Tie The Rapala Loop Knot (ooxBDHQZeUs)

set.description: Joins a heavy leader to a doubled main line. Slim, and it runs through the guides.
set.bestFor: A heavy mono or fluoro leader to a doubled main line (a Bimini twist)
steps: Step 1: Tie a short Bimini twist in the main line to make a doubled line
Step 2: Pass the leader's tag through the loop of doubled line
Step 3: Hold a small loop of leader open with a finger and wrap the leader tag around the doubled line 5 to 7 times
Step 4: Bring the tag back and pass it through the loop your finger holds
Step 5: Wet it and pull the leader and the doubled line to tighten
Step 6: Trim the tag

FishingKnots/bristol-knot.reason: CastAI's Bristol knot is two overhand knots for lines of the same size. That is a different knot. The Bristol knot joins a heavy leader to a doubled line. The Rig Card's first tip (double the wraps on braid) had no source, so there is no tip.
FishingKnots/bristol-knot.source: netknots.com/fishing_knots/bristol-knot; Mercury Marine, How to Tie the Bristol Knot (e2anRbw6-1s)

set.description: Joins a heavy leader or bite tippet to lighter line, slim enough for the guides.
set.bestFor: A heavy leader or bite tippet to lighter main line, braid or mono
steps: Step 1: Tie a loose double overhand knot in the heavy leader so it makes two loops
Step 2: Pass a doubled bight of the main line through both loops
Step 3: Wrap the bight 4 times around the leader, then 4 more turns back over the first four
Step 4: Tuck the bight back under itself
Step 5: Wet it, pull it tight and trim both tags
set.tips: Eight wraps, four out and four back over them. Lay them side by side for a slim knot.

FishingKnots/slim-beauty.reason: CastAI's steps make a loop in the leader and wrap single braid around it, which is closer to an Albright. The Slim Beauty starts with a double overhand in the leader and a doubled main line. CastAI's tip says ten wraps, five on each side, which does not match the corrected steps.

steps: Step 1: Double the line and push the loop through the hook eye
Step 2: Lay the loop back up along the doubled line
Step 3: Working down toward the hook, wrap the loop around both lines 8 times
Step 4: Thread the loop through the gap between the hook eye and the last wrap
Step 5: Wet it and pull the main line, the tag end and the loop to tighten
Step 6: Trim the tag end and the loop

FishingKnots/berkley-braid-knot.reason: CastAI's steps are not Berkley's knot. Berkley ties it with the line doubled, 8 wraps, and the loop through the gap at the eye.
FishingKnots/berkley-braid-knot.source: Berkley Fishing, How to Tie a Berkley Braid Knot (8H88QrRNrKg), steps in the video description

set.description: Joins fly line to backing, or a leader to fly line, with a slim knot that runs through the guides.
set.bestFor: Fly line to backing, or a leader to fly line
steps: Step 1: Lay a small tube or a hollow pen refill alongside the end of the main line
Step 2: Lay the tag end of the backing or the other line alongside them
Step 3: Wrap the tag 6 to 7 times around the tube and both lines, each wrap beside the last
Step 4: Push the tag back through the tube, under the wraps, so it comes out where the wraps began
Step 5: Hold the wraps and slide the tube out. The wraps stay on the lines
Step 6: Wet the knot and pull both ends of the wrapping line to tighten it
Step 7: Trim both tag ends close

FishingKnots/nail-knot.reason: CastAI says it attaches backing to the fly reel. That is the arbor knot. The nail knot joins line to line. No video in CastAI. CastAI's step 4 reads as if the tag goes in at the start, and step 3 leaves out that the wraps go around the tube and both lines.
FishingKnots/nail-knot.source: CastAI's own arbor-knot card (the knot that ties backing to the reel); Terry Corneau nail knot video (nlvIbFhuYcY); video: Terry Corneau, How to tie a nail knot using a tube (nlvIbFhuYcY); animatedknots.com/nail-knot-tube

steps: Step 1: Make a loop by crossing the tag end over the standing line
Step 2: Take the tag around behind the standing line
Step 3: Pass the tag down through the loop from the front
Step 4: Check it shows an 8
Step 5: Pull both ends tight
Step 6: Leave a short tag

FishingKnots/figure-eight-knot.reason: CastAI's steps go under, up through the loop, then over and back through it again, which tangles into an overhand, not an 8.
FishingKnots/figure-eight-knot.source: American Sailing, Figure-Eight Knot, or Stopper Knot (ZEViTAkUbMU)

steps: Let 4 to 5 feet of line hang below the rod tip and hold the rod out at waist to chest height.
Open the bail, hold the line with your index finger, and face your target.
Let the lure swing back like a pendulum. Let its weight do the work.
As it swings forward, smoothly scoop the rod tip upward and forward in an underhand motion.
Let go of the line as the lure swings up toward the target. It arcs out gently.
Finish with the rod pointing at the target, and close the bail once the lure lands.

CastingTechniques/pendulum-cast.reason: CastAI's video (tFvbgu_x204) is the bass pitch, a different cast in this library. This one is South Carolina DNR's underhand cast, which it says to swing as a pendulum: 'allow 4-5 feet of line outside of the rod tip. Use a pendulum motion, release the line on the upswing motion and finish the cast with the rod pointing at the target.' The steps follow it: 4 to 5 feet of line, let go on the upswing (CastAI said 2 to 3 feet, and let go as the lure swings past the rod).
CastingTechniques/pendulum-cast.source: South Carolina DNR, Basic Underhanded Pitch Cast (bibU5cLECPA), its YouTube description; no checked video titled pendulum or underhand swing for a spinning rod was found

set.funFact: Named after Dungeness, a small town on the Olympic Peninsula in Washington.

FishSpecies/dungeness-crab.reason: CastAI adds that Dungeness is "basically the crab capital of the world". No source backs it, so it is cut and the name fact stays.
FishSpecies/dungeness-crab.source: Removal only. The rest of the line is CastAI's.

set.funFact: Steelhead and rainbow trout are the same species. Nobody fully knows why some go to sea and some stay.

FishSpecies/steelhead.reason: CastAI says the two are "genetically identical". They are one species (CastAI's own Oncorhynchus mykiss for both), not identical fish.
FishSpecies/steelhead.source: CastAI FishSpecies.json scientificName for rainbow-trout and steelhead

FishSpecies/rock-crab.reason: CastAI says red rock crab has "incredibly spicy meat". Crab meat is not spicy. Dropped until a checked fact replaces it.

steps: Step 1: Pass the line through the eye and let the lure hang, or pinch the hook in your palm
Step 2: Loop the tag over your index finger and wrap it 7 times around both lines, down toward the eye
Step 3: Pass the tag between the two lines just below the last wrap, by the eye
Step 4: Bring it back up and run it through the loop your finger holds, then take your finger out
Step 5: Wet it, pull the tag tight, then slide the knot down to the lure
Step 6: Trim the tag close

FishingKnots/san-diego-jam.reason: CastAI's steps cross the tag back and wrap it through a loop around both lines: that ties a uni knot, not a San Diego jam. The jam wraps the doubled line toward the eye, then goes between the lines and back through the finger loop. No video in CastAI.
FishingKnots/san-diego-jam.source: netknots.com/fishing_knots/san-diego-jam-knot; video: Fishing with Nat, Tie a San Diego Jam Knot (eiKjTJAfT74)

replace: bring the tag end back toward the bend
bring the tag end back toward the eye
FishingKnots/circle-hook-snell.reason: No video in CastAI. And as on the snell knot, the loop forms when the tag comes back toward the eye, not the bend.
FishingKnots/circle-hook-snell.source: Ultimate Fishing, Circle Hook Knot - The Snell Knot (laFLic70zZM), checked with YouTube oEmbed; animatedknots.com/snell-knot

steps: Step 1: Hold the braid tight (across your thumb and finger, or to the reel) and lay the leader across it
Step 2: Wrap the leader around the braid from behind, then over the front
Step 3: Keep the braid tight and weave the leader around it, alternating sides, until the wraps are about 3/4 inch long
Step 4: Pinch the wraps and tie a half hitch with the braid around the leader and the braid, pull it tight
Step 5: Tie 6 to 8 more half hitches, then pull the braid and leader hard apart to set it
Step 6: Trim the leader close, tie 3 to 4 half hitches of braid around itself, trim, and pull hard to test
set.tips: Keep strong tension on the braid the whole time. Slack braid lets the wraps slide off.

FishingKnots/fg-knot.reason: CastAI makes a loop in the leader and weaves the braid through it. The FG has no loop: the leader is woven around tight braid, then locked with half hitches, which CastAI leaves out. No video in CastAI.
FishingKnots/fg-knot.source: netknots.com/fishing_knots/fg-knot; video: Salt Strong, Easiest Way to Tie the FG Knot (ZPTzkep9xlI)

FishingKnots/albright-knot.source: Fishing with Nat, How to Tie the Albright Fishing Knot (WV2XH0oLs1w), checked with YouTube oEmbed

set.description: Makes a doubled line fast. Not as tough as a Bimini twist, but much quicker to tie.
set.bestFor: A quick double line at the end of the main line
steps: Step 1: Double a length of line and twist a small loop in the doubled line
Step 2: Hold the small loop between thumb and forefinger
Step 3: Wrap the doubled line around your thumb and the loop 5 times (15 on braid)
Step 4: Pass the end of the doubled line through the small loop
Step 5: Pull the doubled line slowly so the wraps unwind off your thumb
Step 6: Wet it and pull all four ends evenly to tighten
set.tips: Let the wraps come off your thumb one at a time, or they tangle.

FishingKnots/spider-hitch.reason: CastAI calls it a loop in the middle of the line for droppers, and its steps wrap a tag around folded strands. The spider hitch doubles the end of the line, wrapped around the thumb. No video in CastAI.
FishingKnots/spider-hitch.source: netknots.com/fishing_knots/spider-hitch; video: Salt Strong, Easiest Way To Tie A Spider Hitch Loop Knot (FXTZxfbc3-Y)

steps: Step 1: Double about 3 feet of line into a long loop and turn the loop to put 20 twists in it
Step 2: Hold the loop open over your knee and keep steady tension on both ends
Step 3: Ease the tag end down so it rolls back over the twists to their end
Step 4: Tie a half hitch around one leg of the loop to lock it, keeping tension on everything
Step 5: Tie 3 to 5 half hitches around both legs of the loop, working back toward the knot
Step 6: Trim the tag to about 1/4 inch

FishingKnots/bimini-twist.reason: CastAI pokes the end loop through the twists and wraps the base. The Bimini rolls the tag back over the 20 twists, then locks with a half hitch and 3 to 5 more around both legs. No video in CastAI.
FishingKnots/bimini-twist.source: netknots.com/fishing_knots/bimini-twist; video: Salt Strong, How To Tie The Bimini Twist Fishing Knot (jMm_zIuAdQE)

FishingKnots/bobber-stop-knot.source: Take Me Fishing, How to Tie a Bobber Stopper Knot (OkEMNssxc4Q), checked with YouTube oEmbed

set.tips: On braid, put mono backing on first, or a strip of electrical tape on the bare spool. Braid spins on a bare spool.

FishingKnots/arbor-knot.reason: No video in CastAI. And no word on braid: braid tied straight to a bare spool with an arbor knot spins, and the Rig Card's river reels carry 30 lb braid.
FishingKnots/arbor-knot.source: Fishing with Nat, How to Tie the Arbor Knot (91tNuE_NNXs), checked with YouTube oEmbed; Tackle Warehouse arbor knot page; Wired2Fish and Outdoor Life on spooling braid (mono backing or tape so it does not spin)

steps: Step 1: Thread the wire through the eye and cross the tag over the standing wire
Step 2: Hold them at more than a right angle and twist both wires around each other at least 3 and a half times
Step 3: Bend the tag to a right angle with the standing wire
Step 4: Wrap the tag tightly around the standing wire about 5 times
Step 5: Bend the tag into a small handle and rock it back and forth until it snaps at the last wrap
Step 6: Check that no sharp end sticks out

FishingKnots/haywire-twist.reason: CastAI wraps the tag 3 times one way, then 3 more the other way. The haywire twist is 3 and a half twists, then about 5 tight barrel wraps one way, then the tag is snapped off. No video in CastAI.
FishingKnots/haywire-twist.source: netknots.com/fishing_knots/haywire-twist; video: BlacktipH, Fishing Tips - Haywire Twist (cEKjXXtmjHM)

CastingTechniques/pitching.source: BassResource, How To Pitch A Fishing Lure (ITuTfvUXhTQ), checked with YouTube oEmbed

CastingTechniques/flipping.reason: No video in CastAI. And CastAI says you miss 80% of your bites if you do not watch the line; no source backs the number.
CastingTechniques/flipping.source: John Crews, How To Flip and Pitch Cast (z8NRFFFUMVY), checked with YouTube oEmbed
replace: Not watching the line on the fall -- you'll miss 80% of your bites
Not watching the line on the fall

CastingTechniques/bow-and-arrow-cast.reason: No video in CastAI. Shown on a fly rod; the same pull and release works on a spinning rod.
CastingTechniques/bow-and-arrow-cast.source: Orvis, Fly Casting Lessons - The Bow And Arrow Cast (zFBdtQfw-ZI), checked with YouTube oEmbed

CastingTechniques/two-handed-spey-cast.source: The New Fly Fisher, Spey Casting Basics (Nl-Qk4jH5II), checked with YouTube oEmbed

CastingTechniques/double-haul.source: Orvis, Fly Casting Lessons - The Double Haul (d8idd4kgXY4), checked with YouTube oEmbed

CastingTechniques/water-haul.source: Orvis, Fly Casting Lessons - Water Haul (ZfPKL1jZDAQ), checked with YouTube oEmbed

CastingTechniques/kayak-cast.source: Saltwater Buffalo Fishing, How to Cast from a Kayak (RpPVF9X4mo8), checked with YouTube oEmbed

CastingTechniques/lob-cast.source: South Carolina DNR, Basic Lob Cast (cJbg5evCcfI), checked with YouTube oEmbed

add.name: Anchor Hitch
add.description: Ties a rope to an anchor ring or chain. Two turns on the ring take the load, so it holds and does not chafe through.
add.bestFor: Anchor line to the anchor ring or the last chain link
steps: Step 1: Pass the end through the ring or chain link twice, making a round turn
Step 2: Take the end around behind the standing part
Step 3: Tuck the end through both turns on the ring
Step 4: Pull the standing part so the turns grip the ring
Step 5: Finish with a half hitch around the standing part
Step 6: Zip tie or tape the tag to the standing part
add.tips: Two full turns on the ring, not one. One turn saws back and forth under load.

FishingKnots/anchor-hitch.reason: CastAI has no rope knots. The Rig Card's kayak anchor card ties the anchor line to the chain with this knot (rigs/content.js, kayak-anchor).
FishingKnots/anchor-hitch.source: InnerBark Outdoors, How to Tie the Anchor Bend Knot (pEWcxx8998U); The Ashley Book of Knots, anchor bend

add.name: Bowline
add.description: A fixed loop in the end of a rope that will not slip or jam, and unties after a load.
add.bestFor: A loop in a rope: the anchor float, a dock line, a tie off
steps: Step 1: Make a small loop in the standing part, with the standing part underneath
Step 2: Pass the end up through the small loop from below
Step 3: Take the end around behind the standing part
Step 4: Bring the end back down through the small loop
Step 5: Hold the end against the side of the big loop and pull the standing part to set it
Step 6: To lock it, tie the end around the side of the big loop with a double overhand
add.tips: A bowline can shake loose when it is not under load, which is why the float end is locked.

FishingKnots/bowline.reason: CastAI has no rope knots. The Rig Card's kayak anchor card puts a locked bowline at the float end (rigs/content.js, kayak-anchor).
FishingKnots/bowline.source: The How To Channel, How to tie a Bowline Knot (eQYVnOWlIZI); The Ashley Book of Knots, bowline

steps: Step 1: Thread 3 to 4 inches of tippet through the hook eye
Step 2: Tie a loose overhand knot with the tag around the standing line, ahead of the hook
Step 3: Bring the tag back through the loop, passing between the overhand knot and the hook
Step 4: Pull the tag first to draw it up, then the main line to set it
Step 5: Trim the tag close

FishingKnots/davy-knot.reason: CastAI stops at the overhand knot. The Davy knot takes the tag back through the loop, between the overhand and the hook; that pass is the knot.

steps: Step 1: Double about 6 inches of line to form a long loop
Step 2: Cross the doubled end over the standing doubled line to make a circle
Step 3: Take the doubled end around behind the standing doubled line
Step 4: Pass it down through the circle from the front. Check it shows an 8
Step 5: Wet it and pull the loop and standing line apart
Step 6: Trim the tag end

FishingKnots/figure-eight-loop.reason: CastAI passes the doubled end under the standing line and then up through the circle. That ties an overhand loop, which is weaker and jams. A figure eight loop is the figure eight knot tied in doubled line: around behind, then down through the circle from the front.
FishingKnots/figure-eight-loop.source: animatedknots.com/figure-8-knot (the same knot in a doubled line)

steps: Step 1: Overlap the braid and the leader by about 8 inches so they run alongside each other
Step 2: Take the braid's tag end, make a loop back along both lines, and wrap through the loop and around both lines 8 times
Step 3: Wet it and pull the tag end to snug that first uni knot down
Step 4: Flip everything and repeat with the leader. Loop, wrap 5 times
Step 5: Wet it and snug the second uni knot
Step 6: Pull both standing lines apart so the two knots slide together and lock against each other
Step 7: Trim both tag ends

FishingKnots/double-uni.reason: CastAI's steps wrap 5 to 6 times on both lines, and its own tip says braid needs 8 and the leader 5. Same wraps on both sides and the braid slips. The tip said the same thing as the card's red box, so it goes.
FishingKnots/double-uni.source: West Marine double uni knot (6 to 8 on braid, 4 to 5 on the leader); takemefishing.org double uni (8 and 4); Tackle Warehouse double uni (the leader side gets about half the braid's wraps)

set.tips: Set the size of the loop by how much line you double at the start.

FishingKnots/surgeons-loop.reason: CastAI's step 1 makes a 4 to 5 inch loop and its tip says 1 to 2 inches works great. The tip now says how to size it without a second number.
FishingKnots/surgeons-loop.source: CastAI FishingKnots.json surgeons-loop, steps and tips

replace: bringing the tag end back toward the bend
bringing the tag end back toward the eye
FishingKnots/snell-knot.reason: The tag end comes through the eye and lies down the shank past the bend. A loop forms when it comes back toward the eye, not the bend.
FishingKnots/snell-knot.source: animatedknots.com/snell-knot; CastAI FishingKnots.json snell-knot steps 1 and 3

steps: Grab the rod with your dominant hand, reel facing down for spinning or up for baitcaster. Firm grip, not a death grip.
Reel in until your lure hangs 6 to 12 inches below the tip, then open the bail or hit the thumb bar.
Hold the line with your index finger (spinning) or thumb on the spool (baitcaster).
Bring the rod straight back to 2 o'clock. Keep it vertical, don't let it drift sideways.
Swing forward in one smooth motion and let go of the line at about 10 o'clock.
Follow through until the rod points at the target, lower the rod tip as the lure hits the water, and close the bail.

CastingTechniques/overhead-cast.reason: CastAI's step 5 says let go at 10 o'clock 'when the rod points at your target', which contradicts itself: at 10 o'clock the rod points up. You let go at 10 o'clock and follow through to the target.
CastingTechniques/overhead-cast.source: takemefishing.org How to Cast (release, then follow through toward the target); CastAI CastingTechniques.json overhead-cast

CastingTechniques/sidearm-cast.reason: CastAI's video (TDJuy2ypTgM) is a sidearm roll cast with a baitcaster, a different motion from this card's flat sweep. Ott DeFoe's is the sidearm sweep itself, for bridges, cover and wind, as the card says.
CastingTechniques/sidearm-cast.source: Ott DeFoe, Ott's Garage | The Side Arm Cast (7Qx4SOjdN-8), checked with YouTube oEmbed; its description: 'A side arm cast is a powerful way to get baits a long way without too much height'

CastingTechniques/pitch-flip.reason: Pitch and flip is the Pitching card and the Flipping card said again in one. One card each, and its names find Flipping, whose video is flipping and pitching.
CastingTechniques/pitch-flip.source: CastAI CastingTechniques.json pitching, flipping and pitch-flip; John Crews, How To Flip and Pitch Cast (z8NRFFFUMVY)

details: Spring-fed, so the water temperature holds steady all year
Sight fishing to big trout in clear water. You can watch them eat
Small flies: sizes 16 to 22, midges and scuds
Fish it from the bank, back from the edge
About 2.5 hours from Bonney Lake, worth the drive

Rocky Ford Creek.reason: CastAI calls it flat, wade-able water to wet wade in shorts. The pamphlet: 'Bank fishing only. Fly fishing only. No wading.'

set.description: Close to home: the Green River gorge above Flaming Geyser State Park. A wadeable river with cutthroat and rainbow trout. About 30 minutes from Bonney Lake.
details: Cutthroat and rainbow trout
Riffle, pool, riffle. Good water for learning to read a river
Walk in at Flaming Geyser State Park
Go in summer and fall
Nymphs: Pheasant Tail and Hare's Ear
set.proTip: Start at Flaming Geyser State Park: easy parking and a mix of water to practice on. Fish the riffles with a nymph rig in the morning.

Green River (Gorge Section).reason: CastAI sends you below Howard Hanson Dam, which is inside the pamphlet's closed stretch (Tacoma Municipal Watershed Boundary Marker, 1.3 miles below the Tacoma Headworks Dam, to Friday Creek: 'CLOSED WATERS'). It says fishable year-round; trout in the open stretches is the Saturday before Memorial Day to Dec 31. 'Stocked rainbow' has no source. Kanaskat-Palmer is not proven to be below the closed stretch, so only Flaming Geyser is named.

set.description: A fly fishing lake on Fidalgo Island near Deception Pass, planted with big rainbow and brown trout.
details: Float tubes, kayaks and rowboats work best. Shore fishing is limited
Damselfly and dragonfly hatches in June bring big fish to the top
Chironomids (midges) under an indicator work most of the year
About 2 hours north of Bonney Lake. Pair it with Deception Pass

Pass Lake (Fidalgo Island).reason: CastAI states the lake's rules as fact, and gets them wrong: 'catch and release, barbless hooks' and 'No spinning gear allowed'. The pamphlet: 'Fly fishing only. Motors prohibited.' and for game fish 'Release all trout.' Rules live on the trip card, not here.

set.description: A small glacial river from Mount Rainier down to Orting, with wild cutthroat. About 20 minutes from Bonney Lake.
details: Wild cutthroat, mostly 8 to 12 inches
Tight and brushy, so roll cast
Small flies: size 14 to 18 nymphs, size 12 to 14 dry flies
Go in summer and fall
set.proTip: Short sessions close to home. Fish a size 14 Elk Hair Caddis in the riffles.

Carbon River.reason: CastAI says it flows right through Bonney Lake (it runs from Carbonado to Orting) and is best in spring. The mouth to Voight Creek is open Sept 1 to Oct 31 only, Voight Creek to the Hwy 162 bridge is closed water, and above that rivers open the Saturday before Memorial Day. 'Access through local parks' is not proven.

replace: Year-round fishery — even winter has good nymphing
Yakima River.reason: 'Year-round fishery' is a rule said as fact. True today (the pamphlet has it year-round, catch and release, selective gear) but rules live on the trip card.

FlyFishingGuide/wa-spots.reason: Rules said as fact in CastAI's Washington spots.
FlyFishingGuide/wa-spots.source: 2026-27 WDFW sport fishing rules pamphlet (eregulations.com/washington/fishing, pages updated Oct 5 2026)

steps: Keep the fish in or right next to the water. A deep-hooked fish is already stressed.
Open the mouth wide (a jaw spreader helps on big fish) and find the hook before you touch anything.
If you can see the hook in the throat, slide your pliers or hook remover down the line to the shank.
Grip the shank, push forward to free the barb, then rotate and back it out.
If it is too deep to see or in the gills, do not force it. Torn gills kill fish.
For catch and release, cut the line as close to the hook as you can. Many fish shed the hook later, and it beats torn gills.
If the rules let you keep this fish, keep it and take the hook out when you clean it.
